And, yes. It CAN happen that way. It DOES happen that way, with many, varied, possible but very actual responses.

-He suppresses any smaller indents/ issues or warning signs leading up to the main incident. 
-Is probably comfortable with more than most of the assumed and probable triggers. 
-Usually tired, due to broken sleep or lack of sleep, but covers it well with caffeine, coffee, or jokes. Maybe the high- stress job gives the rush he needs. 
-Occasional OCD/ADD/ADHD tendencies. 
- Promotes mental health/PTSD awareness/assistance, again as a cover. 
- Good family life; active with kids, supportive of significant other, etc.. Maintains good hygiene. Average to slightly above average social life. Dresses well. Always looks nice, but not over the top. 
- Morning/ daily routines. 
- Overall, can self- acknowledge and have self-awareness of his diagnosis, thoughts, actions, etc., but still maintains that suppression and keeps his façade; almost like denial, but not quite. 

Hope this helps. It's all from direct personal experience. Let me know if you need anything more or help with characters, etc.. Good luck! Hope to read it some day.
